newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds, futures power ahead on U.S. trade data.
newsitem.headline: Bunds, futures power ahead on U.S. trade data.

text.p: German Bunds and futures powered ahead in Thursday afternoon trading, encouraged by a larger-than-expected drop in the U.S. trade deficit in October to $7.99 billion, which boosted U.S. Treasuries.

Higher than forecast weekly U.S. jobless claims at 351,000 and a minus 2.2 reading on the December Philadelphia business index, hinting at a slowdown in the U.S. economy, also helped the bond market extend its gains.
The March DTB Bund future ended up 29 basis points at 100.32, while the 10-year Bund traded at 102.88 to yield 5.83 percent, up from its Wednesday close of 102.55.
Dealers said the Bund future was well supported around 100.12/15.

Earlier in the day news that the Bundesbank had left interest rates unchanged, as expected by most analysts, and that the M3 money supply growth target corridor for 1997 would be 3.5 to 6.5 percent both failed to inspire the market.
The Bundesbank also said its money supply growth target was oriented for two years to cover the run up to European monetary union.
"We could test the week's highs of 100.54/55 on the Bund future, but then we should see profit taking from the five people who are left trading in the market before the weekend," said one dealer.

Dealers said they expected a calm end to the week after Thursday's late rally, saying that neither the probable release of German November producer prices nor the first inflation figures out of key west German states should affect the market too much.
They said the same applied to the release at 1330 GMT of real gross domestic product data out of the U.S.
